title: Steps to Extend Latency in Preterm Prelabor Rupture of Membranes
official: Steps to Extend Latency in Preterm Prelabor Rupture of Membranes
summary:
The goal of this quasi-experimental study is to determine if there are improved outcomes for patients with preterm prelabor rupture of membranes (PPROM) who walk daily. The main question it aims to answer is:

\- Are patients with PPROM who walk at least 3500 steps per day more likely to stay pregnant longer than those who walk less?

Participants will be encouraged to walk ≥3500 steps per day from the time of diagnosis until delivery and their daily step counts will be recorded. Researchers will compare those who actually walk ≥3500 steps per day to those who walk less.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Planned inpatient expectant management of ≥7 days
* Phone capable of monitoring and sharing step count
* Singleton or dichorionic twin gestation

Exclusion Criteria:

* Any records flagged "break the glass" or "research opt out"
* Transverse, footling breech, or funic presentations
* Active preterm labor
* Active vaginal bleeding
